Thought: I need to determine the potential safety risks when epoxides are mixed with toxic metals or metal compounds. Let me analyze this chemistry question.

Epoxides are reactive compounds containing a three-membered ring with an oxygen atom. When mixed with toxic metals or metal compounds, several reactions can occur:

1. Epoxides can undergo ring-opening reactions catalyzed by Lewis acids (which many metal compounds are)
2. This can lead to polymerization reactions
3. Some metal compounds can catalyze violent polymerization of epoxides

Looking at the options, the most significant hazard when epoxides interact with toxic metals or metal compounds is violent polymerization. Epoxides are known to undergo exothermic polymerization reactions when catalyzed by Lewis acids (including many metal compounds), and this polymerization can become violent and uncontrolled.
